title: PIM Activator: create the sign-in app registration
purpose: Creates or updates the PIM Activator app registration in your tenant (the sign-in app of the PIM Activator browser extension): its SPA redirect URIs, its delegated Microsoft Graph and Azure permissions, tenant-wide admin consent for them, and "Assignment required" so only the group you name can sign in.
whenToRun: Once per tenant before the PIM Activator browser extension is rolled out (PIM Manager > Operations > PIM Activator, step 1, shows the command with your values), and again when the extension needs a new permission or you want to change who may sign in. Re-runnable: an existing app with the same display name is updated in place.

runAs.name: Application Administrator
runAs.why: creates / updates the app registration and its service principal. Cloud Application Administrator or Global Administrator also work.

runAs.name: Privileged Role Administrator
runAs.why: only with -GrantConsent (the default): tenant-wide admin consent that includes the protected RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory permission. Global Administrator also works; -GrantConsent:$false skips it.

runAs.name: Delegated sign-in: Application.ReadWrite.All, AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All, DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All
runAs.scope: Microsoft Graph, for the first-party app Microsoft Graph Command Line Tools
runAs.why: the browser sign-in (auth code + PKCE, no extra app) asks for exactly these delegated permissions; they act only within your own roles above. Automation alternatives: -AccessToken with the same scopes, or -AppId + -CertificateThumbprint of an app holding the equivalent application permissions.

changes.object: service principals of the Microsoft first-party APIs Microsoft Graph and Azure Service Management -- only when the tenant does not have them yet
changes.why: the delegated permission ids are read from these service principals; a fresh tenant may not have instantiated them
changes.undo: none needed -- Microsoft first-party service principals; leave them

changes.object: app registration 'PIM Activator' (-DisplayName), single tenant (AzureADMyOrg); updated in place when it exists
changes.why: the extension signs users in with it
changes.undo: delete the app registration (Entra admin center > App registrations > PIM Activator > Delete)

changes.object: SPA redirect URIs https://<extension id>.chromiumapp.org/ and chrome-extension://<extension id>/ (merged with the URIs already there; public-client URIs cleared). -Channel Both / Test also adds the TEST build's id (internal tenants only)
changes.why: launchWebAuthFlow returns to the chromiumapp.org URI; Entra validates the extension origin on token redemption
changes.undo: remove the URIs under Authentication, or delete the app registration

changes.object: required permissions (delegated): Microsoft Graph PrivilegedAccess.ReadWrite.AzureADGroup, Group.Read.All, User.Read, RoleManagement.Read.Directory, RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory, AdministrativeUnit.Read.All, Application.Read.All; Azure Service Management user_impersonation
changes.why: what the extension needs to list and activate PIM eligibilities (groups, Entra roles, Azure roles) and to find this app in its setup wizard. PrivilegedAccess.Read.AzureADGroup is not enough: activation needs ReadWrite.
changes.undo: remove them under API permissions, or delete the app registration

changes.why: the tenant's instance of the app: consent, assignment and 'Assignment required' live on it

only the people you assign can sign in; nobody else can get its tokens. An app that is open to everyone and has nobody assigned is not closed without -AssignToGroupId (that would lock every current user out).
changes.undo: Enterprise applications > PIM Activator > Properties > Assignment required = No

changes.permission: Default access -- an app role assignment (appRoleId 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000), not an application permission
changes.scope: the PIM Activator enterprise application only
changes.why: who may sign in to the PIM Activator; an id that is not a group is refused and the assignment removed again
changes.undo: Enterprise applications > PIM Activator > Users and groups > remove the group

changes.object: tenant-wide admin consent (oauth2PermissionGrant, consentType AllPrincipals) from 'PIM Activator' to Microsoft Graph
changes.permission: delegated: PrivilegedAccess.ReadWrite.AzureADGroup Group.Read.All User.Read RoleManagement.Read.Directory RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory AdministrativeUnit.Read.All Application.Read.All openid profile offline_access
changes.scope: all users of the tenant -- in practice only the assigned group can sign in; a delegated permission acts only within the signed-in user's own rights
changes.why: users are not asked to consent one by one (with -GrantConsent, the default)
changes.undo: Enterprise applications > PIM Activator > Permissions > revoke, or delete the oauth2PermissionGrant

changes.object: tenant-wide admin consent (oauth2PermissionGrant, AllPrincipals) from 'PIM Activator' to Azure Service Management
changes.scope: all users of the tenant (only the assigned group can sign in); acts only within the user's own Azure rights
changes.why: the extension lists and activates the user's Azure role eligibilities
changes.undo: Enterprise applications > PIM Activator > Permissions > revoke

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.default: the home tenant of the account you sign in with
parameters.help: Your tenant id; the sign-in is refused when it lands in another tenant. Required for app-only sign-in.

parameters.name: AssignToGroupId
parameters.help: Object id of the group whose direct members may use the PIM Activator. Not given: nobody can sign in until a group is assigned.

parameters.name: Channel
parameters.help: Released registers only the released extension id. Both / Test also register the TEST build (internal tenants only).

parameters.name: DisplayName
parameters.help: Display name of the app registration (also how an existing one is found).

parameters.name: ExtensionId
parameters.help: The extension id; change it only for a fork of the extension.

parameters.name: GrantConsent
parameters.help: Grant tenant-wide admin consent. -GrantConsent:$false skips it (users or an approver consent later).

parameters.name: UseEdge
parameters.help: Open the sign-in in Microsoft Edge (the default browser when Edge is missing). -UseEdge:$false uses the default browser.

parameters.name: AccessToken
parameters.help: Automation: a Microsoft Graph token you already have, with the delegated scopes above. Skips the browser sign-in.

parameters.name: AppId
parameters.help: Automation, app-only: client id of an app holding Application.ReadWrite.All (+ DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All for consent) as application permissions. Use with -CertificateThumbprint and -TenantId. Not used by the command PIM Manager shows.

parameters.name: CertificateThumbprint
parameters.help: Automation, app-only: thumbprint of that app's certificate in the local certificate store. Not used by the command PIM Manager shows.

readsOnly: your own sign-in (/me) and your active Entra roles (from the token, or /me/memberOf)
the published permission ids of the Microsoft Graph and Azure Service Management service principals
app registrations named -DisplayName, and the enterprise application's current assignments and 'Assignment required' setting
existing admin-consent grants of the app
whatIf: Signs in, reads the tenant, and prints a 'What if:' line for every change: the app registration it would create or update (with its redirect URIs and permissions), the service principal it would create, the group it would assign, 'Assignment required', and the two admin-consent grants. Nothing is written.
undo: Delete the app registration 'PIM Activator' in the Entra admin center (App registrations > PIM Activator > Delete): that removes its service principal, its group assignment and its consent grants with it. The PIM Activator extension can then no longer sign in.
